items.t: Premenstrual syndrome (including premenstrual tension and depression); puerperal depression; luteal phase support as part of assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment.

src.q: Treatment of premenstrual syndrome, including premenstrual tension and depression. 2) Treatment of puerperal depression. 3) Luteal phase support as part of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) treatment for women.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPC accessed. The SmPC says it is not indicated in threatened miscarriage (see cautions).

items.t: Premenstrual syndrome and puerperal depression: 200 mg daily up to 400 mg twice a day, vaginally or rectally. Premenstrual syndrome: start on day 14 of the cycle (day 12 if symptoms are present at ovulation) and continue until menstruation starts.

src.q: 200mg daily to 400mg twice a day, by vaginal or rectal insertion
For premenstrual syndrome commence treatment on day 14 of menstrual cycle and continue treatment until onset of menstruation. If symptoms are present at ovulation commence treatment on day 12.

items.t: Luteal phase support (ART): 400 mg vaginally twice a day from oocyte retrieval; if pregnancy is confirmed, continue for 38 days.

src.q: 400 mg administered vaginally twice a day starting at oocyte retrieval. The administration of Cyclogest should be continued for 38 days, if pregnancy has been confirmed.

items.t: No experience in liver or renal impairment; no clinical data over 65 years.

src.q: There is no experience with use of Cyclogest in patients with impaired liver or renal function.
No clinical data have been collected in patients over age 65.

items.t: No relevant use in children.

src.q: There is no relevant use of Cyclogest in the paediatric population.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to progesterone or any excipient; undiagnosed vaginal bleeding; known or suspected progesterone-sensitive malignant tumours; porphyria.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. - Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. - Known or suspected progesterone sensitive malignant tumours. - Porphyria.

items.t: Severe hepatic dysfunction or disease; known missed abortion or ectopic pregnancy; active arterial or venous thromboembolism or severe thrombophlebitis, or a history of these.

src.q: Severe hepatic dysfunction or disease - Known missed abortion or ectopic pregnancy. - Active arterial or venous thromboembolism or severe thrombophlebitis, or a history of these events.

items.t: Not indicated in threatened miscarriage; stop if a missed miscarriage occurs.

src.q: Cyclogest is not indicated in threatened miscarriage. Treatment should be discontinued in the event of a missed miscarriage.

items.t: Stop if myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular disorder, arterial or venous thromboembolism, thrombophlebitis or retinal thrombosis is suspected. In women with thromboembolic risk factors (e.g. personal or family history), weigh benefit against risk.

src.q: Cyclogest should be discontinued if any of the following conditions are suspected: myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular disorders, arterial or venous thromboembolism (venous thromboembolism or pulmonary embolism), thrombophlebitis or retinal thrombosis.
In these women, the benefits of Cyclogest administration need to be weighed against the risks.

items.t: History of depression: observe closely and consider stopping if symptoms worsen.

src.q: Drugs known to induce the hepatic cytochrome-P450-3A4 system (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine or phenytoin) may increase the elimination rate and thereby decrease the bioavailability of progesterone.

items.t: Other vaginal products at the same time: effect on progesterone exposure not assessed, so not recommended.

src.q: The effect of concomitant vaginal products on the exposure of progesterone from Cyclogest has not been assessed and is therefore not recommended.

items.t: Contraindicated in severe hepatic dysfunction or disease. Use with caution in other hepatic dysfunction (metabolised in the liver).

src.q: Severe hepatic dysfunction or disease
Progesterone is metabolised in the liver and should be used with caution in patients with hepatic dysfunction.

items.t: Should not be used in pregnancy, except in the first trimester as part of ART treatment (luteal support). Data on congenital anomalies are limited and inconclusive.

src.q: Cyclogest should not be used during pregnancy except as indicated during the first trimester of pregnancy for use as part of an assisted reproduction (ART) treatment
There is limited and inconclusive data on the risk of congenital anomalies

items.t: Progesterone passes into breast milk; should not be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: Progesterone is excreted in human milk and Cyclogest should not be used during breast-feeding

items.t: Premenstrual syndrome and puerperal depression: use rectally if barrier contraception is used.

src.q: Use rectally if barrier methods of contraception are used.

items.t: Common: somnolence, abdominal pain or discomfort, breast pain. Frequency not known: diarrhoea and flatulence with rectal use; periods may come earlier (or, more rarely, later) than expected; local soreness and leakage.

src.q: SYSTEM ORGAN CLASS Common Uncommon Not known Nervous system disorder Somnolence Gastrointestinal disorders Abdominal pain, Abdominal discomfort
Diarrhoea and flatulence may occur with rectal administration.
Menstruation may occur earlier than expected, or, more rarely, menstruation may be delayed.

items.t: Insert vaginally or rectally. Use rectally with barrier contraception, vaginal infection (especially thrush), recurrent cystitis or after recent childbirth; use vaginally with colitis or faecal incontinence. ART luteal support is vaginal.

src.q: Use rectally if patients suffer from vaginal infection (especially moniliasis) or recurrent cystitis or have recently given birth. Use vaginally if patients suffer from colitis or faecal incontinence.
